text: The serpent stone is a round bit of glass with magical power. It also is called the serpent's egg, druid's glass, serpent bead, adder stone, Clach Nathrach, and Glaine Nathair. Of all methods of divination and healing open to the Druids, this one was the most powerful and the most secret. The Roman Pliny wrote that a warrior of the Vocontian Gauls died on Claudius's order for bearing an ovum anguinum, a serpent's egg, into court. The stone could form only in summer at a set phase of the moon, when many snakes writhed about one another and raised a ball of liquid into the air. The same mad serpents chased any thief, halted only by running water. Pliny claimed one egg as large as an apple, though most were the size of a nut. The stone helped in lawsuits and healed. One dipped in a glass of water cured bewitchment. Long after the Druids, folk still called it treasured medicine. In the 19th century people found serpent stones in heather, where a snake had drooled spittle in a circle.
